risk_analysis.scope: GDPR posture and EU data residency, vendor lock-in and exit costs, migration risk, hidden-cost risk, and support risk for Salesforce, HubSpot and Zoho CRM, evaluated for Brightline (40-person ad agency, Dublin, Ireland).
assumptions: Knowledge cutoff early 2026; no live web verification. Pricing, data-centre locations and certifications should be re-confirmed contractually before signing.
Brightline processes EU personal data (client contacts, campaign audiences) and is the data controller; the CRM vendor is a processor under Art. 28 GDPR.
Brightline has no dedicated CRM admin today and a small IT footprint.
Current contact data lives in spreadsheets and a legacy mailbox-based workflow; no prior CRM to decommission.

gdpr_data_residency.salesforce: Strong compliance machinery: standard DPA with SCCs, EU Data Residency add-on and Hyperforce EU Operating Zone (EU-located processing and EU-based support access). Caveats: full EU Operating Zone is a paid premium historically aimed at enterprise tiers, and Salesforce remains a US-headquartered company, so Schrems-II / EU-US Data Privacy Framework dependency persists. Best-in-class paperwork; residency guarantees cost extra.
gdpr_data_residency.hubspot: Offers an EU data hosting option (Frankfurt, AWS eu-central-1) selectable at account creation — it cannot be switched later without a migration, so Brightline must choose EU hosting on day one. DPA, SCCs and DPF participation are standard. Some sub-processors and support access may still be non-EU; acceptable for an ad agency, but document it in the RoPA.
gdpr_data_residency.zoho: Operates its own EU data centres (Amsterdam and Dublin) and stores EU-signup customer data in the EU by default — strongest default residency story, and Zoho runs its own infrastructure rather than US hyperscalers. Compliance documentation and audit reporting are thinner than Salesforce's; legal review of the DPA takes more effort.
gdpr_data_residency.shared_risk: All three are adequate for GDPR with correct configuration. The dominant residual risk is configuration error by Brightline (e.g., HubSpot account created in US region, marketing consent fields unmapped), not vendor non-compliance.

vendor_lock_in_exit.salesforce: Highest lock-in. Proprietary Apex/Flow customisations, ecosystem add-ons and multi-year contracts with auto-renewal and steep renewal uplifts. Data export is possible (weekly export, APIs) but rebuilding automations elsewhere is expensive. Exit cost: high (estimated 2-4 months of consultant effort if customised).
vendor_lock_in_exit.hubspot: Moderate lock-in. Good export APIs and CSV export, but workflows, reporting and the marketing-hub coupling (lists, forms, email history) do not transfer. Annual prepaid contracts; seat-tier downgrades restricted mid-term. Exit cost: moderate (weeks).
vendor_lock_in_exit.zoho: Lowest lock-in. Month-to-month available, full data export, modest customisation surface. Exit cost: low, mostly data-cleansing labour.

risk_analysis.migration_risk: Greenfield migration (spreadsheets to CRM) is low-to-moderate risk for all three. Per-vendor: Salesforce carries implementation-partner dependency and scope-creep risk — a 40-person agency rarely succeeds with self-service setup. HubSpot has the best guided onboarding for this segment; mandatory paid onboarding (~EUR 1.5-3k for Professional) is actually a risk mitigant. Zoho is self-service friendly but data-import tooling and dedupe are cruder, raising data-quality risk. Universal mitigation: appoint one internal data owner, dedupe before import, and migrate in two waves (contacts/companies first, deals second).

hidden_cost_risk.salesforce: Severe. Per-seat price is only the start: required add-ons (CPQ, marketing, integration via MuleSoft or third parties), API call limits, sandbox costs, premier support (~30% uplift), and consultant fees. Realistic TCO is commonly 2-3x licence cost.
hidden_cost_risk.hubspot: Moderate. Marketing Hub pricing scales on contact count — an ad agency holding large prospect/audience lists can see costs jump at contact-tier thresholds. Onboarding fees and Sales/Marketing hub split licensing surprise buyers.
hidden_cost_risk.zoho: Low-moderate. Cheap seats, but advanced features push you toward Zoho One bundle; per-feature gaps trigger third-party tool spend (enrichment, e-sign), and integration glue work is borne internally.

support_risk.salesforce: Standard support is slow without paid Premier tier; SMBs are low priority. Mitigate via partner retainer.
support_risk.hubspot: Phone/chat support included on Professional tier and generally well rated; large knowledge base and Dublin-based EMEA presence (HubSpot's EMEA HQ is in Dublin) — a practical advantage for Brightline's timezone and hiring of experienced admins locally.
support_risk.zoho: Weakest support reputation: slower response, timezone friction, paid premium support tiers needed for guaranteed SLAs. Mitigate with a local Zoho partner or accept longer resolution times.

risk_register.risk: EU data residency not enabled at account creation; cannot be retrofitted without migration
risk_register.mitigation: Select EU (Frankfurt) data hosting when provisioning the account; verify region in account settings before any data import.

risk_register.risk: Multi-year contract with auto-renewal and renewal-price uplift creates exit barrier
risk_register.mitigation: Negotiate 1-year initial term, renewal cap clause, and written data-egress assistance terms before signature.

risk_register.risk: TCO blowout from add-ons, API limits and consultant dependency
risk_register.mitigation: Demand a 3-year all-in TCO quote including add-ons and partner fees; compare against budget ceiling before shortlisting.

risk_register.risk: Contact-tier pricing escalation as marketing/audience lists grow
risk_register.mitigation: Track marketing-contact count monthly; mark non-marketing contacts as such (not billed); archive stale lists quarterly.

risk_register.risk: Slow support resolution blocking campaign-critical workflows
risk_register.mitigation: Budget for Zoho premium support or a local partner retainer; keep documented workarounds for known issues.

risk_register.risk: Data-quality degradation during spreadsheet import (duplicates, bad consent flags)
risk_register.mitigation: Pre-import dedupe and consent-field audit; two-wave migration; named internal data owner signs off each wave.

risk_register.risk: GDPR consent/lawful-basis fields misconfigured, exposing Brightline to controller liability
risk_register.mitigation: Map consent capture into CRM fields during onboarding; run a DPIA-lite review; enable built-in GDPR tooling (deletion, subject-access export).

risk_register.risk: Workflow/automation lock-in making future exit expensive
risk_register.mitigation: Document all workflows outside the tool; prefer standard properties over heavy customisation; annual export drill.

risk_register.risk: Thinner compliance documentation lengthens client security reviews (agencies get vendor-audited by clients)
risk_register.mitigation: Collect Zoho's SOC 2 / ISO 27001 certificates and DPA up front; keep a pre-filled vendor-security answer pack.

risk_register.risk: Implementation stalls without dedicated admin; shelfware risk
risk_register.mitigation: If Salesforce is chosen, contract a certified partner and name an internal admin (0.5 FTE); otherwise prefer a lighter platform.

risk_analysis.risk_verdict: From a pure risk standpoint: Salesforce concentrates cost, lock-in and implementation risk that a 40-person agency cannot easily absorb, despite the strongest compliance paperwork. Zoho minimises cost and lock-in risk but carries the highest support and compliance-documentation friction. HubSpot is the balanced-risk choice: credible EU hosting (provided the Frankfurt region is selected at signup), bounded exit costs, Dublin-based EMEA support presence, and hidden costs that are real but predictable and controllable via contact-list hygiene.
